headline: Gorbachev meets Pope John Paul II at the Vatican
summary: On 1 December 1989 Mikhail Gorbachev visited the Vatican and met Pope John Paul II, the first meeting between a Soviet leader and a pope.
significance: The two agreed to establish relations, and Gorbachev promised freedom of conscience in the USSR, including for Ukraine's suppressed Greek Catholic church.

headline: Ukraine votes for independence
summary: On 1 December 1991 over ninety per cent of voters in Ukraine approved the declaration of independence, and Leonid Kravchuk was elected president.
significance: Without Ukraine, the Soviet Union could not survive; within a week its leaders met at Belovezha to dissolve it.

headline: Four American churchwomen murdered in El Salvador
summary: On 2 December 1980 four American churchwomen, three nuns and a lay missioner, were abducted and murdered by members of El Salvador's National Guard.
significance: The killings caused President Carter to suspend aid to El Salvador briefly and made the Salvadoran military's abuses a lasting issue in Congress.

headline: Bush and Gorbachev meet off Malta
summary: On 2-3 December 1989 George Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev held their first summit aboard ships off Malta, weeks after the Berlin Wall opened.
significance: The Malta summit is often taken as the moment the two leaders declared the Cold War over.

headline: Pablo Escobar killed in Medellin
summary: On 2 December 1993 Colombian police tracked down and killed the Medellin cartel leader Pablo Escobar on a rooftop in Medellin.
significance: The hunt, assisted by US intelligence and special forces, ended the cartel's campaign of bombings against the Colombian state.

headline: Gas leak at Union Carbide plant kills thousands in Bhopal
summary: On the night of 2-3 December 1984 methyl isocyanate gas leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, killing thousands.
significance: The world's worst industrial disaster put an American corporation's conduct abroad on trial.

headline: East German Politburo resigns
summary: On 3 December 1989 the entire Politburo and Central Committee of East Germany's ruling party resigned, and Erich Honecker and other former leaders were expelled from the party.
significance: The party's collapse left the GDR state without its leadership weeks after the Wall opened.

headline: Carapintada officers rise against Argentina's government
summary: On 3 December 1990 rebel army officers loyal to Colonel Mohamed Ali Seineldin seized army headquarters in Buenos Aires. Loyal troops put down the uprising within a day, at a cost of over a dozen lives.
significance: It was the last of the 'carapintada' rebellions against civilian rule, and came on the eve of a visit by President Bush.

headline: Kuwait Airways flight hijacked to Tehran; two Americans killed
summary: On 4 December 1984 hijackers seized a Kuwait Airways flight and forced it to Tehran, where they killed two US AID officials. Iranian security forces stormed the plane on 9 December.
significance: The hijackers demanded the release of the Dawa prisoners held in Kuwait for the 1983 bombings, including of the US Embassy; Washington accused Tehran of complicity.

headline: Terry Anderson, the longest-held American hostage, is freed
summary: On 4 December 1991 Islamic Jihad released Terry Anderson, the Associated Press correspondent kidnapped in Beirut in March 1985.
significance: Anderson's release after nearly seven years effectively ended the Lebanon hostage crisis that had drawn the Reagan administration into the Iran-Contra affair.

headline: Soviet Union and Afghanistan sign a friendship treaty
summary: On 5 December 1978 Afghan leader Nur Mohammad Taraki and Leonid Brezhnev signed a twenty-year Treaty of Friendship, Good-Neighbourliness and Cooperation in Moscow.
significance: Moscow later cited the treaty as the legal basis for its invasion of Afghanistan a year later.

headline: Warsaw Pact leaders meet in Moscow on the Polish crisis
summary: On 5 December 1980 the leaders of the Warsaw Pact states met in Moscow to discuss the crisis in Poland, amid Western fears of a Soviet invasion.
significance: US intelligence, warned by the CIA's agent in the Polish general staff, Ryszard Kuklinski, judged an intervention possible; President Carter publicly warned Moscow.

headline: Budapest memorandum on Ukraine's nuclear disarmament
summary: On 5 December 1994 at a CSCE summit in Budapest, the United States, Britain and Russia signed memoranda giving security assurances to Ukraine, Belarus and Kazakhstan in return for giving up their Soviet nuclear weapons.
significance: The agreement removed the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal from Ukraine.

headline: Truck bomb hits Colombia's security police headquarters
summary: On 6 December 1989 a truck bomb exploded outside the headquarters of Colombia's Administrative Department of Security (DAS) in Bogota, killing over sixty people. It was aimed at the DAS director, Miguel Maza Marquez, who survived.
significance: The Medellin cartel's attack on the state security service was one of the bloodiest of its war against extradition to the United States.

headline: Hindu activists destroy the Babri mosque at Ayodhya
summary: On 6 December 1992 Hindu nationalist crowds demolished the sixteenth-century Babri mosque at Ayodhya in northern India.
significance: The demolition set off riots across India that killed some two thousand people and strained relations with Pakistan.

headline: Earthquake devastates Soviet Armenia
summary: On 7 December 1988 an earthquake struck northern Armenia, destroying Spitak and much of Leninakan and killing about 25,000 people.
significance: Gorbachev cut short his visit to the United States, and for the first time the Soviet Union accepted large-scale Western aid, including from America.

headline: Gorbachev announces troop cuts at the United Nations
summary: On 7 December 1988 Mikhail Gorbachev told the UN General Assembly that the Soviet Union would cut its armed forces by half a million men, including withdrawals from Eastern Europe.
significance: The unilateral cuts signalled Moscow would no longer hold Eastern Europe by force.

headline: Reagan and Gorbachev sign the INF Treaty
summary: On 8 December 1987 Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty in Washington.
significance: The treaty eliminated an entire class of nuclear missiles, with intrusive on-site inspections that broke new ground in verification.

headline: Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agree to dissolve the USSR
summary: On 8 December 1991 the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, meeting at Belovezha near Brest, declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist and formed the Commonwealth of Independent States.
significance: The agreement ended the Soviet Union in all but name; Gorbachev resigned seventeen days later.

headline: First Palestinian intifada begins in Gaza
summary: On 9 December 1987, after an Israeli truck collided with cars carrying Palestinian workers in Gaza, protests spread into a general uprising in the occupied territories.
significance: The intifada brought the Palestinian question back to the centre of world politics and led the US to open a dialogue with the PLO a year later.

headline: Lech Walesa elected president of Poland
summary: On 9 December 1990 Lech Walesa, the Solidarity leader, won Poland's presidential run-off election against Stanislaw Tyminski.
significance: The electrician who led the 1980 strikes became head of state ten years later.

headline: Raul Alfonsin inaugurated, ending military rule in Argentina
summary: On 10 December 1983 Raul Alfonsin was sworn in as president of Argentina, ending seven years of military rule.
significance: He soon decreed the prosecution of the junta leaders for the disappearances.

headline: Czechoslovakia gets a non-communist government; Husak resigns
summary: On 10 December 1989 President Gustav Husak swore in a government with a non-communist majority, then resigned.
significance: Husak had presided over the 'normalisation' after the 1968 invasion; his departure cleared the way for Havel's election.

headline: Russian forces enter Chechnya
summary: On 11 December 1994 Russian troops moved into Chechnya to crush its declared independence.
significance: The war became a disaster for the Russian army and Boris Yeltsin.

headline: NATO adopts the double-track decision on Euromissiles
summary: On 12 December 1979 NATO ministers in Brussels decided to deploy US Pershing II and cruise missiles in Western Europe from 1983, while offering arms control talks on intermediate-range missiles.
significance: The decision answered the Soviet SS-20 and set off the Euromissile crisis of the early 1980s.

headline: Russia votes on a new constitution; Zhirinovsky's party surges
summary: On 12 December 1993 Russians approved a new presidential constitution and elected a new parliament, in which Vladimir Zhirinovsky's Liberal Democratic Party won the largest share of the party-list vote.
significance: The constitution entrenched Yeltsin's power after the October crisis, but the nationalist vote alarmed the West.

headline: Martial law declared in Poland
summary: On 13 December 1981 General Wojciech Jaruzelski declared martial law in Poland; Solidarity's leaders were interned and the army and security forces took control.
significance: The crackdown had been prepared in secret; the CIA had been forewarned by its agent on the Polish general staff, Colonel Ryszard Kuklinski, who had been exfiltrated weeks before. Washington imposed sanctions on Poland and the USSR.

headline: Israel extends its law to the Golan Heights
summary: On 14 December 1981 the Knesset passed the Golan Heights Law, applying Israeli law and administration to the territory captured from Syria in 1967.
significance: The effective annexation led the Reagan administration to suspend a newly signed strategic cooperation agreement with Israel.

headline: Bosnian peace agreement signed in Paris
summary: On 14 December 1995 the leaders of Bosnia, Croatia and Serbia formally signed the Dayton peace agreement in Paris.
significance: The signing ended the Bosnian war and handed peacekeeping to a NATO-led force including US troops.

headline: US and China announce they will establish diplomatic relations
summary: On 15 December 1978 President Carter and the Chinese government announced that the United States and the People's Republic of China would establish full diplomatic relations on 1 January 1979.
significance: Normalisation, with the end of US recognition of Taiwan, completed the strategic opening to China against the Soviet Union.

headline: Moscow replaces Kazakhstan's Kunayev, setting off riots in Alma-Ata
summary: On 16 December 1986 Moscow replaced Kazakhstan's party leader Dinmukhamed Kunayev with Gennadiy Kolbin, a Russian; Kazakh students protested in Alma-Ata the next day and the protests were put down by force.
significance: It was the first major outbreak of national unrest of the Gorbachev era.

headline: Kazakhstan declares independence
summary: On 16 December 1991 Kazakhstan declared independence, the last Soviet republic to do so.
significance: Kazakhstan held a large share of the Soviet nuclear arsenal.

headline: Red Brigades kidnap US General James Dozier
summary: On 17 December 1981 Red Brigades terrorists kidnapped US Army Brigadier General James Dozier, a NATO officer, from his flat in Verona.
significance: Dozier was the first American general kidnapped by European terrorists; Italian police rescued him unharmed on 28 January 1982.

headline: Romanian security forces fire on protesters in Timisoara
summary: On 17 December 1989 Romanian army and Securitate forces opened fire on demonstrators in Timisoara, where protests had begun over the attempted eviction of the pastor Laszlo Tokes.
significance: The massacre set off the revolution that overthrew Nicolae Ceausescu within a week.

headline: Fernando Collor elected president of Brazil
summary: On 17 December 1989 Fernando Collor de Mello defeated Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil's first direct presidential election since 1960.
significance: Collor's election completed Brazil's return to democracy; he was impeached three years later.

headline: Ceausescu leaves on a visit to Iran amid the Timisoara crisis
summary: On 18 December 1989 Nicolae Ceausescu left Bucharest for a state visit to Iran, while his security forces were putting down the uprising in Timisoara.
significance: He cut the visit short and returned on 20 December to a regime days from collapse.

headline: Kim Young-sam elected president of South Korea
summary: On 18 December 1992 Kim Young-sam won South Korea's presidential election, becoming its first civilian president in three decades.
significance: His government curbed the military and the intelligence service and prosecuted former presidents Chun and Roh.

headline: Britain and China sign the Hong Kong agreement
summary: On 19 December 1984 Margaret Thatcher and Zhao Ziyang signed the Sino-British Joint Declaration, under which Hong Kong would return to China in 1997.
significance: The agreement set out the 'one country, two systems' formula.

headline: Moscow announces Sakharov may return from exile
summary: On 19 December 1986 the Soviet government announced that Andrey Sakharov could return to Moscow from internal exile in Gorkiy, where he had been watched by the KGB since 1980.
significance: Sakharov's release was the most visible sign that Gorbachev's reforms extended to the treatment of dissidents.

headline: United States invades Panama to oust Noriega
summary: On 20 December 1989 US forces invaded Panama to remove General Manuel Noriega, the country's ruler and a former intelligence chief who had for years been a paid CIA asset.
significance: Operation Just Cause, the largest US combat operation since Vietnam, ended in Noriega's surrender and trial in Miami on drug charges.

headline: Shevardnadze resigns, warning of coming dictatorship
summary: On 20 December 1990 Soviet Foreign Minister Eduard Shevardnadze resigned in a speech to the Congress of People's Deputies, warning that dictatorship was approaching.
significance: Shevardnadze had been Washington's partner in ending the Cold War. His warning proved prescient: hard-liners attempted a coup eight months later.

headline: Pan Am flight 103 destroyed over Lockerbie
summary: On 21 December 1988 a bomb destroyed Pan Am flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing all 259 aboard and 11 people on the ground.
significance: Investigators later charged two Libyan intelligence officers with the bombing, and it became the defining case of state-sponsored terrorism of the era.

headline: Ceausescu is shouted down at a Bucharest rally
summary: On 21 December 1989 a mass rally called by Nicolae Ceausescu in Bucharest turned against him, and fighting broke out in the capital that night.
significance: The televised moment the crowd jeered him marked the end of his regime.

headline: Eleven republics join the Commonwealth at Alma-Ata
summary: On 21 December 1991 the leaders of eleven Soviet republics met in Alma-Ata and agreed to form the Commonwealth of Independent States.
significance: The Alma-Ata declaration sealed the end of the USSR; Gorbachev resigned four days later.

headline: Ceausescu flees Bucharest as the Romanian revolution triumphs
summary: On 22 December 1989 Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu fled the Central Committee building in Bucharest by helicopter as the army went over to the crowds. Fighting with Securitate loyalists continued for days.
significance: Romania's was the only violent overthrow of a communist regime in Eastern Europe in 1989.

headline: Andrey Sakharov returns to Moscow from exile
summary: On 23 December 1986 Andrey Sakharov and Yelena Bonner returned to Moscow by train after nearly seven years of internal exile in Gorkiy.
significance: His return gave Gorbachev's glasnost credibility abroad and brought the leading Soviet dissident back into public life.

headline: Slovenians vote for independence
summary: On 23 December 1990 Slovenians voted overwhelmingly in a plebiscite for independence from Yugoslavia.
significance: The vote set the course for the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1991.

headline: Noriega takes refuge in the Vatican's embassy in Panama
summary: On 24 December 1989 General Manuel Noriega, hunted by US forces, took refuge in the Vatican's nunciature in Panama City.
significance: US troops surrounded the building and blared loud music at it; Noriega surrendered on 3 January 1990.

headline: GIA hijacks Air France flight 8969 in Algiers
summary: On 24 December 1994 gunmen of Algeria's Armed Islamic Group seized an Air France Airbus at Algiers airport. French gendarmes stormed it in Marseille two days later.
significance: The hijackers were believed to have intended to crash the plane into Paris.

headline: Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu tried and executed
summary: On 25 December 1989 Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu were tried by a hastily convened military tribunal at Targoviste and shot.
significance: Their execution was meant to end Securitate resistance; footage was shown on Romanian television the next day.

headline: Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
summary: On 25 December 1991 Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as President of the USSR in a televised address, and the Soviet flag was lowered over the Kremlin.
significance: The end of the Soviet Union closed the Cold War.

headline: Supreme Soviet votes the USSR out of existence
summary: On 26 December 1991 the Soviet of the Republics of the USSR Supreme Soviet adopted a declaration recognising that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist.
significance: It was the formal end of the Soviet state.

headline: Islamic Salvation Front leads Algeria's first-round vote
summary: On 26 December 1991 the Islamic Salvation Front won a clear lead in the first round of Algeria's parliamentary elections.
significance: The army cancelled the second round in January 1992, setting off a decade of civil war.

headline: Soviet special forces storm Amin's palace in Kabul
summary: On 27 December 1979 Soviet KGB and military special forces stormed the Tajbeg palace in Kabul and killed Afghan leader Hafizullah Amin; Babrak Karmal was installed in his place.
significance: The operation, disguised at first as an Afghan affair, was the opening act of the Soviet war in Afghanistan.

headline: Abu Nidal gunmen attack Rome and Vienna airports
summary: On 27 December 1985 gunmen of the Abu Nidal Organisation attacked El Al and TWA check-in counters at Rome and Vienna airports, killing nineteen people including five Americans.
significance: Washington blamed Libya for supporting the attackers, imposing sanctions in January and leading to the US bombing of Libya in April 1986.

headline: Alexander Dubcek elected chairman of the Czechoslovak parliament
summary: On 28 December 1989 Alexander Dubcek, leader of the 1968 Prague Spring, was elected chairman of the Federal Assembly of Czechoslovakia.
significance: The return of the man deposed by the Soviet invasion completed the symbolism of the Velvet Revolution.

headline: Vaclav Havel elected president of Czechoslovakia
summary: On 29 December 1989 the Federal Assembly unanimously elected the dissident playwright Vaclav Havel president of Czechoslovakia.
significance: A man imprisoned by the regime months earlier became head of state; under Havel, Czechoslovakia opened the files of its secret police, the StB.

headline: Israel and the Vatican agree to establish relations
summary: On 30 December 1993 Israel and the Holy See signed a Fundamental Agreement in Jerusalem leading to full diplomatic relations.
significance: The agreement ended decades of Vatican non-recognition of Israel.

headline: Jerry Rawlings seizes power again in Ghana
summary: On 31 December 1981 Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings overthrew Ghana's elected President Hilla Limann, two years after he had handed power to civilians.
significance: Rawlings would rule Ghana until 2001.

headline: Military coup in Nigeria
summary: On 31 December 1983 the Nigerian army overthrew President Shehu Shagari's civilian government; Major General Muhammadu Buhari became head of state.
significance: The coup ended Nigeria's Second Republic.

headline: Czechoslovakia dissolves at midnight
summary: At midnight on 31 December 1992 Czechoslovakia ceased to exist, peacefully dividing into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
significance: The 'velvet divorce' contrasted sharply with the bloody breakup of Yugoslavia.
